newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Chronology of events in Serbian elections.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of events in Serbian elections.

text.p: Serbia has been shaken by a wave of street protests this month that started after the opposition accused President Slobodan Milosevic's ruling Socialists of committing poll fraud to overturn results of local elections.
Here is a chronology of related events:

Nov 3 - President Milosevic's leftist coalition, led by his ruling Socialist party, wins comfortable victory in federal elections, securing majority in Yugoslav parliament. In parallel local elections, run-off polling was required in most municipalities in Serbia.
Nov 17 - Second round for municipal polls held in municipalities where no candidate managed to obtain a majority.

Nov 18 - Zajedno (Together) coalition of opposition parties claims victory in the capital Belgrade and 15 of the country's biggest towns in stunning blow to ruling Socialists. Zajedno leaders cite evidence from their representatives on electoral commissions.
- Ruling Socialists claim victory in 134 of 189 councils. The Socialists' victory list does not include the major towns that the opposition says it won.
- After opposition victory rally in Belgrade, supporters march to city hall where Zajedno leaders warn electoral officials against tampering with results.
- Demonstrations begin in southern town of Nis where supporters suspect authorities will cancel Zajedno victory.
Nov 19 - Opposition holds another rally and Belgrade electoral commission confirms Zajedno victory in the capital.
- Zoran Djindjic, an opposition leader and head of the Democratic Party, is touted to become the first non-communist mayor of Belgrade since World War Two.
- Tensions rise in Nis and other towns after electoral commissons fail to announce final results within 48 hours after close of polling stations as required by law.
- Authorities, citing irregularites reported by Socialist Party, begin to annul results in Nis and several other towns.

Nov 20 - Zajedno leaders call on supporters to defend their victories as protests continue in Belgrade and other towns. Zajedno shows documents to Western diplomats which it says proves election victory.
Nov 21 - Some 20,000 march in support of Zajedno in Belgrade as leaders vow to organise daily protests until election victory is recognised.
- In first public response to opposition protests, Socialists accuse Zajedno of "prematurely" declaring victory and accuse leadership of inciting violence.
Nov 24 - Belgrade municipal court, annuls opposition victory in city council.
Nov 25 - University students launch strike in Belgrade faculties. Some 100,000 opposition supporters attend Belgrade demonstration, the biggest yet.
Nov 26 - Supreme Court rejects appeal from opposition lawyers on annulment of poll results.
Nov 27 - Vuk Draskovic, a leader of Zajedno coalition, calls for Milosevic's resignation at demonstration.
- Authorities stage third round of voting in towns where courts annulled results. Opposition boycotts third round in Belgrade but participates elsewhere.
- Belgrade independent radio station B-92 says its signal repeatedly jammed.
Nov 28 - Socialists say they secured majority in Belgrade assembly after third round which Zajedno denounces as a sham.
Dec 1 - Belgrade police say they have been more tolerant than required and warn against further protests which they say are violent and illegal.
- Serbian speaker of parliament, Dragan Tomic, delivers harsh attack on opposition on state television, calling Zajedno "pro-fascist" and comparing leaders to Adolf Hitler.
Dec 3 - Authorities switch off transmitter broadcasting independent Radio B-92 and student-run Radio Index.
- United States and European states condemn the move. Washington says "outer wall" of sanctions against Belgrade will remain in place until Serbia shows respect for democracy.
Dec 4 - Serbia promises U.S. it will not to resort to force to stop protests, in meeting between Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic and Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott,
- The unpopular Socialist party chief in Nis, Mile Ilic, resigns in concession to opposition protests, state media says.
- Authorities say "technical teams" are examining why Radio B-92 went off the air.
